headline: WHEATON PRECIOUS METALS POSTS RECORD Q2 — $929M Revenue, $543M Net Earnings, Both Up ~85% YoY; $3,875/GEO Cash Margin; Antamina Silver Stream Drives Silver To 52% Of Revenue (NYSE/TSX: WPM)
snippet: Wheaton Precious Metals Corp. (NYSE/TSX: WPM) reported record Q2 2026 financial results on August 7, delivering revenue of approximately $929 million and net earnings of $543 million — both up roughly 85% year-over-year — as the company's royalty and streaming model captured the full benefit of gold at $4,300+ and silver at $64+. The Antamina silver stream, one of the largest silver streaming agreements in the industry, drove silver to approximately 52% of total revenue — a striking reversal from recent quarters when gold dominated. Cash margin per gold equivalent ounce reached $3,875, a figure that would have seemed implausible when Wheaton's portfolio deals were structured. For retail investors in streaming and royalty companies, Wheaton's Q2 illustrates the operating leverage these structures provide at elevated metals prices: with no operating cost exposure to inflation, AISC escalation, or permitting delays, Wheaton's margin expansion is nearly dollar-for-dollar with the gold and silver price moves since January. At a $4,300 gold equivalent price and with over 40 streams and royalties across multiple jurisdictions, record-breaking quarters are becoming the base case — not the exception.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC SILVER Q2: 217% DIVIDEND HIKE, $195M FREE CASH FLOW — $415.5M Revenue (+57%), AISC $25.68/AgEq; $1.25B Treasury; Silver Is Back (NYSE: AG)
snippet: First Majestic Silver Corp. (NYSE: AG, TSX: FR) reported Q2 2026 results on August 7, posting revenue of $415.5 million — a 57% year-over-year increase — with free cash flow of $195 million and a 217% increase to its quarterly dividend, reflecting the transformative impact of silver at $64+ per ounce on the company's Mexican and US silver-gold operations. All-in sustaining costs of $25.68 per silver equivalent ounce generated margins above $38/oz at current silver prices. The company's treasury stands at approximately $1.25 billion — a war chest that positions First Majestic as a potential acquirer in a market where junior silver developers are still trading at fractions of their in-ground value. The 217% dividend hike signals management's confidence that current silver prices are sustainable, not a spike. For retail investors tracking primary silver producers, First Majestic's Q2 is the clearest demonstration yet that six consecutive annual supply deficits are printing in company cash flows: the Silver Institute's 46-million-ounce projected 2026 deficit is not an abstract forecast — it is showing up as margin expansion in every silver producer's results this earnings season.

headline: COEUR MINING Q2: RECORD $1.1B REVENUE; GOLD OUTPUT +51% ON NEW AFTON AND RAINY RIVER — $388M FCF, $1.1B Cash (10x YoY); Guidance Cut 3 Months On Ramp-Up Delays (NYSE: CDE)
snippet: Coeur Mining Inc. (NYSE: CDE) reported Q2 2026 results with record revenue of $1.1 billion — driven by a 51% year-over-year increase in gold production following the integration of the New Afton and Rainy River assets — alongside free cash flow of $388 million and a cash balance of $1.1 billion, approximately 10 times the year-ago figure. The cash transformation is the headline: Coeur entered 2025 as a heavily leveraged mid-tier with balance sheet risk; it exits Q2 2026 as a net cash company generating nearly $400 million in quarterly free cash flow. The counterpoint is a guidance reduction of approximately three months across key operations — a ramp-up timing issue rather than a reserve or geotechnical problem, but one that the market will watch closely into Q3. For investors tracking the mid-tier gold consolidation theme, Coeur's Q2 illustrates both the upside of transformative acquisitions at the right point in the gold cycle and the execution risk that comes with integrating multiple new assets simultaneously at record throughput rates.

headline: THOR EXPLORATIONS CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE GOLD 400m BELOW SEGILOLA PIT — 19.4m At 3.01 g/t Au From 346m; New Steeply-Dipping Shoot; Underground Study Advancing; Nigeria (TSX-V/AIM: THX)
snippet: Thor Explorations Ltd. (TSX-V/AIM: THX) announced August 6, 2026 drill results from below the Segilola Gold Mine open pit in Osun State, Nigeria — confirming a new steeply-dipping high-grade gold shoot at depth with a headline intercept of 19.4 metres at 3.01 g/t gold from 346 metres downhole, including 4.7 metres at 6.79 g/t Au, approximately 400 metres below the current pit floor. This represents the first confirmation that Segilola's high-grade gold system — which delivered steady open-pit production at grades above 4 g/t — persists at depth in a geometry amenable to underground mining. A preliminary underground scoping study is now advancing. For investors in African-focused gold producers, underground extensions below high-grade open pits represent the highest-value exploration outcome: the infrastructure, permits, and mine camp already exist; underground access would require incremental capital against a defined, high-grade target rather than a greenfield construction. At $4,300+ gold, a 3 g/t underground intercept 400 metres below an existing pit carries meaningfully more NAV than the same result would have at $2,000 gold.

headline: ACHILLES DEEPEST HOLE HITS 26m At 102 g/t AgEq From 433m — 250m Below Current MRE Base; 2m Core At 770 g/t; System Open 540m Down Dip; Exploration Upside Material (ASX: AGC)
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper Limited (ASX: AGC) reported this week that its deepest drill hole to date at the Achilles deposit — part of the Boda-Kaiser Project in New South Wales — returned 26 metres at 102 g/t silver equivalent from 433 metres depth, including a 2-metre high-grade core at 770 g/t AgEq, extending known mineralization approximately 250 metres below the current mineral resource estimate base and leaving the system open to 540 metres vertically down dip. The Achilles deposit is part of a large polymetallic porphyry-related system that Australian Gold and Copper has been systematically drilling since 2024; the depth extension confirms that the system's high-grade core is not constrained by a shallow cut-off — a critical differentiation for any future resource calculation that will now need to model additional tonnes at depth. At silver above $64 per ounce, AgEq grades above 100 g/t over 26 metres at 433 metres depth represent an economically meaningful underground intercept. For ASX-listed junior investors, depth extensions that materially exceed the current MRE base are the category of drill result most likely to drive resource category upgrades in the next estimate update.

headline: QUEENSLAND URANIUM TAILINGS HIDE WORLD-CLASS REE DEPOSIT — JCU Scientists: 7Mt At 3% REE At Mary Kathleen; Top-25 Grade Globally; Zero New Mining Required
snippet: Research published in August 2026 by scientists at James Cook University revealed that uranium mine tailings at the historic Mary Kathleen site in Queensland, Australia contain approximately 7 million tonnes of rare earth element-bearing material at an average grade of approximately 3% total REE — placing the deposit among the top 25 highest-grade known REE occurrences globally, and requiring no new mining: the material has already been extracted and sits in surface storage from historical uranium operations. The Mary Kathleen mine operated from 1958 to 1982 and left behind significant tailings that were never processed for their rare earth content, which was of minimal economic interest at the time. At current REE prices — particularly for the critical magnet metals neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium — a 7-million-tonne surface tailings deposit at 3% total REE in a Tier-1 Australian jurisdiction is potentially a development-ready critical minerals project. For investors in Australian critical minerals, reprocessing of historical tailings carries a fundamentally different permitting and community acceptance profile than greenfield mining — and represents a category of REE resource that could reach production in years rather than decades.

headline: ZIJIN MINING H1 2026: NET PROFIT +68% TO RMB 39.1B — Mine Gold +15%, Copper +11%, Lithium +514%; World's #3 Miner By Market Cap Tops $100B
snippet: Zijin Mining Group Co. Ltd. reported H1 2026 net profit of approximately RMB 39.1 billion (approximately US$5.4 billion) — a 68% year-over-year increase — driven by a 15% increase in mine gold production, 11% increase in copper output, and a 514% surge in lithium production as its newly commissioned lithium assets moved to full run-rate. Zijin has surpassed Rio Tinto and BHP in market capitalization to become the world's third-largest mining company by that measure, with a market cap exceeding US$100 billion. The Northern Miner profiles Zijin's aggressive multi-commodity expansion as the template for how a state-backed Chinese miner with a low cost of capital has outmaneuvered Western majors on asset acquisition timing: Zijin bought copper, gold, and lithium assets during the 2015–2020 commodity downturn at valuations that now look transformative. For Western junior investors, Zijin's H1 results are a benchmark for what the commodity environment is worth: $5.4 billion in net profit in six months from assets that were considered speculative acquisitions a decade ago is the clearest possible signal that current metals prices are rewriting asset values across the entire mining spectrum.

headline: GOLD-SILVER FORECASTS ALREADY BLOWN THROUGH — August Consensus Was $3,800-$4,350 Gold, $55-$62 Silver; NFP Jobs Miss Rewrites September FOMC Odds; Where Do Analysts Stand Now?
snippet: CBS News surveyed leading bullion analysts and fund managers for August 2026 price forecasts — a consensus that projected gold between $3,800 and $4,350 per ounce and silver between $55 and $62 — and then watched the NFP miss of minus-23,000 jobs blow through the top of the range within hours of publication. The article canvasses revised analyst commentary: those who had modelled a $4,300 ceiling are now publishing new targets of $4,500 to $4,800 for Q3, citing the combination of a structurally weaker US labour market, the Federal Reserve's asymmetric response function (more likely to cut than hike from here), and gold's demonstrated willingness to hold every multi-week consolidation as a launching pad for the next leg higher. Silver's implied targets — $68 to $75 for Q3 — are even more bullish relative to current spot, reflecting the supply deficit dynamic that separates silver's fundamental case from gold's safe-haven story. For mining investors, the practical takeaway is that sell-side consensus, which is the input most institutional fund managers use for NAV modelling, is still running significantly below current spot — meaning the average resource company is being modelled on assumptions that the market has already invalidated.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM STOCK SELLOFF IS RISK-OFF, NOT FUNDAMENTAL — Long-Term Price Hits $94/lb 18-Year High While URNM Falls 3.9% H1; 81.4M Lbs In Physical Trust; Buy The Dislocation
snippet: Sprott Asset Management published analysis arguing that the 3.9% first-half decline in the URNM uranium equities ETF — against a backdrop where the long-term uranium contract price rose to $94 per pound, its highest level in 18 years — represents one of the most significant fundamental dislocations in the commodity equity space. Sprott's Uranium Physical Trust now holds 81.4 million pounds of physical uranium, providing a floor bid for the spot market independent of equities sentiment. The firm's thesis: uranium stocks sold off in H1 2026 alongside the broader risk-off rotation that hit speculative equities, but the operational and contract fundamentals underpinning uranium's multi-year bull market — reactor restarts in Japan and South Korea, new builds in emerging markets, US domestic enrichment policy, and the structural gap between identified mine supply and projected reactor demand — have not changed. For retail investors in uranium equities, the divergence between spot contract prices (18-year highs) and stock prices (down year-to-date) is either a generational mispricing or a signal that equities are correctly anticipating a spot price correction. Sprott's case is the former: the physical uranium bid and long-term contract price are the more reliable signal.

headline: GOLD ABOVE $4,350 POST-NFP: TECHNICAL OUTLOOK — $4,400 Resistance Now Key; $4,200 Becomes New Floor If Weekly Close Holds; Silver Targets $68 On Breakout (FX Empire)
snippet: FX Empire's August 7, 2026 technical forecast for gold and silver argues that the NFP-driven surge above $4,350 has materially shifted the short-term chart structure: gold has closed above both the June-August consolidation range and the key $4,334 resistance level that FOREX.com identified as the bulls' line in the sand, and a weekly close above $4,350 would establish $4,200 as the new structural floor rather than a ceiling. The analysis identifies $4,400 as the next meaningful resistance — a psychological round number coinciding with a previous intraday high — and projects that a sustained break above it opens a measured-move target of $4,600 before year-end. For silver, the move above $64 has held the $60 structural floor confirmed across multiple tests since June and targets a breakout to $68 if the gold-silver ratio continues to compress from its current elevated level (approximately 68:1 vs. a historical average of 50:1). For mining stock investors, the technical analysis framing matters because institutional flows into gold mining ETFs (GDX, GDXJ) are partially driven by systematic trend-following strategies that trigger above defined breakout levels — meaning a sustained close above $4,400 gold could catalyse a secondary institutional inflow into the equity sector that has lagged the metal year-to-date.
